title: Sections over an algebraically closed point are exact on the pro-etale site
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], whose final object is $\operatorname{id}:s\to s$. Then the functor $\Gamma(s,-):\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(s)$ from abelian sheaves on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to abelian groups is exact: every surjection of abelian sheaves $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ gives a surjection $\mathcal F(s)\to\mathcal G(s)$. Consequently, for every sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal A$ on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the functor $\Gamma(s,-)$ from $\mathcal A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] to $\Gamma(s,\mathcal A)$-modules is exact; applied termwise to complexes it preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so it induces a functor $\Gamma(s,-):D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal A)\to D(\Gamma(s,\mathcal A))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] commuting with shifts and carrying distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category], and $H^i(\Gamma(s,K))=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^i(K))$ for every $K$ and $i$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

source.place: lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected (Tag 0982) and lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible (Tag 098H), applied to A = k (Spec k is w-local, pi_0 a point, k strictly henselian); stated for the big site in Stacks; needed by literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-admissible/def-weil-finite-coefficient-point.md

proof.text: The spectrum of a field has just the prime ideal $(0)$, so $s$ and its connected-component space are one-point spaces. Its closed-point set is the whole space and its sole component has one closed point; thus it is w-local. The closure of either open subset of its component space is open, so that space is extremally disconnected. The sole maximal localization is $k$ itself. Its maximal ideal is zero, so for every finite $k$-algebra $B$ the quotient $B/0B=B$ makes the idempotent lifting condition the identity. Thus $k$ is henselian. An irreducible polynomial over an algebraically closed field has a root and therefore has degree one; in particular the residue field $k$ has no nontrivial finite separable extension. It is separably closed, and $k$ is strictly henselian.

source.place: Tag 0982, lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected, condition (3), specialized to a field; henselian terminology: algebra.tex Tag 04GF and more-algebra.tex Tag 09XI.

proof.text: Apply the geometric retraction criterion to $R=k$, using the three conditions established in step 1. It gives, for every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map $f:k\to B$, a ring map $r:B\to k$ with $r\circ f=\mathrm{id}_k$. This supplies exactly the ring-theoretic hypothesis needed for weak contractibility; no finite-presentation assumption on $B$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0982, lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected, (3) implies (1), with the definition of w-contractible rings, Tag 0981.

proof.text: In the full small site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ take $X=T=s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with structural map the identity. Apply the affine weak-contractibility theorem to the retractions from step 2. For every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on this very site, $F(s)\to G(s)$ is surjective. Thus its affine final object $s$ is weakly contractible. The cited statement is explicitly on the small site, so no restriction of an arbitrary small-site sheaf to or from the big site is being presumed. The existing Lean theorem permits set-valued sheaves in Type (max u (t+1)) independently of the scheme universe t; apply it with these universe parameters.

source.place: Tag 098H, lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible, (1) implies (2); its covering and open-and-closed gluing argument on the small site is recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: For any commutative ring sheaf A with values in universe max u (t+1), let R be its underlying ring sheaf and ev the actual module-evaluation functor at the final object. Forgetting module structure preserves finite colimits, hence epimorphisms, by the source-library instance SheafOfModules.preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf (the exactness clause of lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful). An epic module-sheaf map therefore gives an epic abelian-sheaf map. The general-site abelian epimorphism criterion makes it locally surjective. Forgetting to sets preserves the local lifts and hence gives an epimorphism of set sheaves. Step 3 makes its component at the final object surjective, which is precisely the underlying function of ev.map f. ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective proves that ev preserves epimorphisms. Evaluation preserves kernels sectionwise; Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels then gives preservation of homology, and consequently of finite limits and finite colimits. No coproduct or arbitrary-colimit assertion is needed, nor any bound on the coefficient universe beyond containing the site.

source.place: Tag 0946 (1), exactness from weak contractibility, together with sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA and 03DB for the exact forgetful functor. Lean follows the proof of weaklyContractible_evaluation_preservesHomology with independent coefficient universes.

proof.text: An epimorphism f of abelian sheaves is locally surjective by the general-site abelian-sheaf epimorphism criterion. Apply sheafCompose with the forgetful functor to sets. Its underlying component functions and image sieves are unchanged, so its local surjectivity follows from that of f; the set-sheaf epimorphism criterion makes the resulting morphism epic. Step 3 applied to this morphism proves surjectivity of f on sections of the final object. This uses no constant integer sheaf or extension of an integer action across sheafification.

source.place: Tag 03CN, lemma-abelian-abelian, part (5), and sites.tex Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves; forgetting operations leaves the local lifting condition unchanged.

proof.text: Apply preservation of homology by an exact functor to $\Phi=\Gamma(s,-)$ from step 4 and the three consecutive terms $K^{i-1}\to K^i\to K^{i+1}$ of any complex. The natural isomorphism of that theorem identifies the quotient of cycles by boundaries in the section complex with $\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^i(K))$. Thus $H^i(\Gamma(s,K))\cong\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^i(K))$ in every integer degree. Naturality gives, for a quasi-isomorphism $u:K\to L$, the identification of $H^i(\Gamma(s,u))$ with $\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^i(u))$. The latter is an isomorphism because $\mathcal H^i(u)$ is, proving preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, with no boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; apply its kernel, image and homology consequences degree by degree.

proof.text: Finally apply the exact-functor derived factorization theorem to the exact additive functor of step 4. Both categories are abelian, the source being the category of module sheaves on the small skeleton specified in the pro-etale-site definition and the target an ordinary module category. The theorem gives a functor on their unbounded derived categories, represented by the termwise section complex, together with its shift comparisons and triangulated structure. Therefore it commutes with shifts and sends distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. For any representative of a derived object $K$, step 6 computes its cohomology; naturality and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms make this a canonical identification $H^i(\Gamma(s,K))\cong\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^i(K))$ independent of the representative. The equality in the statement denotes this canonical isomorphism. In Lean, reuse the already proved CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso (in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.ExactFunctor), reversed to match the required orientation; its proof descends the natural homology comparison by localization and allows arbitrary derived-category universes.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, (3)-(4), and Tag 014X, lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category; the cited factorization includes the descended shift and triangle structures.
